correctness.rationale: Direct unitary Fourier change of basis produces the block triangular matrix [[A,B],[0,I]] with A=[[a,b],[b,a]], row Gram BB* fixed by norms and c. Orthogonal parity diagonalization gives the exact two quadratic factors and N-4 unit entries. a>b>0 proves invertibility for all permitted parameters. The midpoint Dirichlet derivative yields K_N exactly, the odd small eigenvalue has even eta expansion, and the even high eigenvalue yields C_N. The checker independently constructs 40 full Gram matrices, all matching to 1.38e-14, and tests four asymptotic coefficients. Finite tests are supplemental.

value.rationale: At the critical square Fourier sampling density, a physically natural two-neighbor collision is a controlled superresolution test. The theorem classifies every spectral direction rather than only providing a generic conditioning inequality, isolates just four exceptional levels in arbitrarily large matrices, and computes a sharp matrix-size-dependent inverse-gap coefficient with nontrivial universal limit. The precise noise-amplification prefactor is useful where general oversampled cluster theorems are inapplicable; the result is not an arbitrary finite parameter tabulation.
